body: Refuse the restore with Error::Configuration unless the snapshot's provider_class_id and endpoint fields (default_base_url, base_url_env, api_key_env, config_envs) equal the registered provider's Instead: Take the endpoint fields from the registered provider too and ignore the snapshot's, so every restore succeeds but a snapshot's custom base URL is silently replaced.
rests_on: The automated security review of commit 7deefbf found that ProviderRegistry::restore_provider (src/providers/base.rs) copies the registered provider's api_key_value, env and headers into whatever endpoint the snapshot names; a snapshot edited to set default_base_url to https://attacker.example would send the live key there. MOD-004 requires taking credentials from the registry but says nothing about the endpoint; refusing a mismatch keeps a snapshot's meaning explicit and fails loudly, while MOD-004's falsifier (same-endpoint restore carries sk-live) still holds.
title: How should Model::from_value stop a tampered snapshot from sending the registered provider's API key to another host?
wrong_if: An application that restores a snapshot of a provider whose base URL legitimately differs from the provider registered under that name gets a configuration error and must register that provider under its own name.

subject: restore_provider refuses a snapshot whose provider class or endpoint fields differ from the registered provider's (commit a84c7f9, test restore_refuses_snapshots_that_would_send_credentials_elsewhere)

body: Add Tool::with_strict(bool) and Tool::is_strict(), keeping the flag as strict: true in the function tool's tool_config args, so no public struct gains a field Instead: Add strict to ToolSpec with a serde default; every struct literal of ToolSpec outside the crate stops compiling.
rests_on: src/types/tools.rs: Tool and ToolSpec are public structs with public fields and no non_exhaustive marker, and the tests and docs build them as literals (ToolSpec { description, params }), so a new field breaks every such literal; Tool::validate_shape already allows tool_config on a function tool, and the OpenAI and Anthropic converters ignore it for function tools (src/providers/openai/tools.rs convert). TypeScript keeps strict on the function tool itself (google-prepare-tools.ts).
title: How does a caller mark a function tool strict, which GGL-007 turns into the Gemini mode VALIDATED, given that the crate's Tool and ToolSpec have no strict field?
wrong_if: The flag lives in a field documented for provider-executed tools, so a reader of a serialized tool has to know that strict: true in a function tool's tool_config args means a strict function.

body: Keep the sources, once per URL, in the final message's provider metadata under google.sources, each in the TypeScript source shape (sourceType url or document, id, url, title, mediaType, filename) Instead: Add a Source part and event to the core types; that changes the Part and Event enums every adapter, the hydrator, replay and the UI adapters match on.
rests_on: src/types/messages.rs Part has Text, ToolCall, ToolResult, BuiltinToolCall, BuiltinToolReturn, Reasoning, Hook and File only, and src/types/events.rs Event has no source event; the Python SDK 0.8.0 core these types port has no source part either (tests/fixtures/ui-python-0.8.0.json only passes UI source-url parts through). GGL-008 and GGL-028 say only that grounding chunks and annotations become sources once per URL, and GGL-009 already puts groundingMetadata in the final metadata under google, so a sources list there needs no core change.
title: How should the Gemini and Interactions readers deliver the sources GGL-008, GGL-028 and GGL-029 require, given that the crate's Part and Event types have no source kind?
wrong_if: An application that wants sources as message parts, for example to render citations inline in the UI adapter, has to read them from provider metadata, and a later core Source part would move them.

subject: Tool::with_strict(bool) and Tool::is_strict() in src/types/tools.rs keep the flag as strict: true in a function tool's tool_config args; google/tools.rs sends functionCallingConfig mode VALIDATED when a function tool is strict (GGL-007); no public struct gained a field

google/response.rs (generate content) and google/interactions/output.rs (Interactions) put the sources once per URL in the final message's provider metadata under google.sources, each in the TypeScript source shape (sourceType url or document, id, url, title, mediaType, filename); no Part or Event kind was added. Test ggl_008_grounding_sources_are_kept_once_per_url
